# Phase 0 — Repository Audit

Performed before any modification, per the operating rules. Subject: `cuda_guard_engine.py` (1,513 lines, single file, no `tests/`, no `docs/`, no package manifest — everything built and manually verified via direct execution across prior sessions, not via a persisted test suite).

| Existing component | What it does | Correct | Incomplete | Misleading | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `detect_environment()` | Fingerprints Python/torch/CUDA/pynvml/gcc/SDK availability | Yes | No OS/CPU/RAM fields the new diagnostics command wants | No | **Reuse**, extend fields |
| `AuditLedger` | Append-only in-memory event list + external-evidence hook | Yes, for what it claims | No hash chaining, no tamper detection, no integrity verification | Not currently — never claimed tamper-evidence | **Replace** with hash-chained ledger; keep the `record()`/`record_external_evidence()` call signatures so nothing downstream breaks |
| Module 1 `InferenceOnlyGovernor` | Monkeypatches `.backward()`/`.step()` across all `Optimizer` subclasses | Yes — subclass-walk fix verified in an earlier session (patching only the base class silently misses SGD/Adam) | No formal, persisted bypass-test suite (verification so far was ad hoc, not re-runnable) | Slightly — raises `GovernanceViolationError`, which reads as proof of a violation rather than "training-shaped API call observed" | **Reuse** logic; **add** persisted bypass tests; **rename** evidence wording |
| Module 2 `DriverInterceptor` | Compiles a real LD_PRELOAD C shim, proves interception via subprocess+harness | Yes — actually tested with real dynamic linking, not asserted | No tests for alternative bypass paths (static link, unobserved process) | No — already scoped correctly ("this process was observed," not "all GPU activity") | **Reuse** as-is; **add** the missing bypass tests |
| Module 3 attestation (`NRASAttestationAdapter`, `TEEAttestationEngine`, `AttestationMode`) | Real `nv-attestation-sdk` integration, gated to Hopper+, bounded-timeout, EAT claim parsing | Yes — tested against the real installed SDK, including the 30s-hang fix | Terminology mostly aligned already; lacks explicit `HARDWARE_ATTESTATION_UNAVAILABLE` for the pre-attempt-skip case (currently folded into `SIMULATED_*`) | No — `HARDWARE_BACKED_ATTEST_FAILED` vs. absence-of-evidence was already correctly separated in a prior session | **Reuse** almost entirely; reconcile one terminology gap |
| Module 4 (`HardwareRegistry`, `FlopLedger`, `NVMLAuditor`) | Registry check, GEMM FLOP ledger via real hooks, NVML query w/ emulated fallback | Yes | Registry schema is thin (uuid/whitelisted/blacklisted only) vs. the signed-registry schema now required; `FlopLedger.total_flops` risks being read as total device FLOPs | Mildly — nothing currently states "lower bound" explicitly in the field name | **Reuse** hook logic; **replace** registry schema; **rename** FLOP fields |
| Module 5 `ModelSpecRegistry` | SHA-256 hash of sorted state_dict, registry lookup | Yes, for the one case tested | No persisted test matrix (reordered dict, dtype change, missing/extra tensor, post-check replacement) | No — a docstring already states the "proves identity at measurement time, not continuity" limitation | **Reuse**; **add** test matrix; **add** before/during/after continuity tracking |
| Module 6 `ComputeBudgetTracker` | R&D/deployment FLOP split + ratio-limit check | Yes | Category is accepted as given, no explicit `evidence_supporting_declaration` field | No — Trust Architecture doc already states this is self-reported | **Reuse**; **extend** schema |
| Module 7 `NCCLAuditor` | Software size-threshold heuristic on `torch.distributed` collectives | Yes, and self-documents its own heuristic limitation | No formal bypass tests | No | **Reuse**; **add** tests; network evidence (new) is a separate, complementary source, not a replacement |
| Module 8 (`DeterminismEngine`, `TimeLockAttestation`) | Deterministic-mode config, monotonic+nonce signing | Yes | — | No — `TimeLockAttestation`'s key is already documented as in-process/not-independently-rooted, matching what Section 37 demands | **Reuse** as-is |
| `GovernanceVerdict` / `LayerFinding` / `EvidenceLayer` | Five-layer combination, built last session | Yes, tested | Status vocabulary is informal (`available: bool` + free text) vs. the richer required vocabulary (`VERIFICATION_SUPPORTED`, `successful_checks`, `unsupported_claims`, etc.) | No | **Reuse** the combination skeleton; **replace** internal vocabulary/fields |
| `main()` CLI | One linear demo script (a→h) | Yes, as a demo | Not a real multi-subcommand CLI | No — never claimed to be | **Replace** with a real subcommand CLI; **reuse** every underlying call it makes |
| *(absent)* | — | — | PCAP/network evidence, recomputation framework, memory-wipe interface, capability registry, formal red-team module, `tests/`, `docs/`, package manifest all do not exist yet | — | **Add**, per priority order below |

**Headline finding from this audit, stated plainly:** every real capability built in prior sessions has actually held up under re-inspection — nothing here needed to be walked back. The two structural gaps are (1) no persisted, re-runnable test suite (verification happened, but lived in scrollback, not in a `tests/` directory), and (2) the evidence/verdict vocabulary is closer to this spec's intent than to its letter — the underlying discipline was already there, the formal enum states weren't. Both are being fixed as part of this pass, not deferred.
